findings.claim: The closure contract used to anchor landing_commit to the commit that landed the delivery 'onto the default branch'. This change replaces that with 'the selected integration branch', and nothing in the skill says who selects that branch or how. That changes what t1 means for actuals and roadmap consumers. With feature-branch-chain delivery, the 'last slice to land' lands on the intermediate feature branch, so the parent can now name that commit. Its committer timestamp comes before the change reaches the default branch, which shortens the elapsed time t0→t1 without any disclosure. The new test only rejects the old wording and does not pin which branch qualifies.
